speaker: Doctor
text: How would you describe the location and nature of your knee pain? Is it localized to one specific spot, or is it more diffuse across the joint?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old female. The patient presents with knee pain that started yesterday and has been steadily worsening. She cites recent participation in volleyball involving repetitive pivoting and twisting movements as a possible cause. She was advised at her last physical exam that weight loss could be beneficial for her health.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is a significant detail. Did you hear a "pop" or "snap" sound at the moment the pain started, and does the knee currently give way when you try to stand or walk?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Knee pain, specifically over the medial aspect of the tibia just inferior to the patella. I also have Recent weight loss attempt, Increased physical activity.

speaker: Doctor
text:
REQUEST TEST: Knee_X-Ray_appraisal for osteochondritis dissecans or stress fracture.  
REQUEST IMAGES: MRI_knee_coronal_sagittal for meniscal tear or osteochondritis dissecans.  
Please tell me if you have any swelling or locking sensation in the joint, and whether the pain radiates down your calf.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Polycystic ovarian syndrome (PCOS), currently managed with oral contraceptive pills. Social history: Has recently joined a volleyball team.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies any fever, recent injuries, swelling or discoloration of the knee, or previous similar complaints. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Medial Tibial Stress Syndrome (Shin Splints).
